The principle of philanthropy is simple: when someone 
gives, someone else receives. In between, there is 
an invisible thread that connects a troubled student 
to a youth worker, a mother to her child, an immigrant 
to a resource person, a senior to a trainer, and so on. 
The Y brings together countless people, stimulates 
communication, opens hearts, and inspires ideas and 


projects. 


There are strong forces at work at the Y, and actions being taken that change lives forever. 


Messea5e from The YMCAs of Quebec 


What a year for The YMCAs of Québec! Looking back, 2008 was a year 
marked by a strategic renewal during which we adopted a five-year plan and 
took many significant actions. 


First, the YMCA of Greater Montreal changed its name to The YMCAs of 
Québec, thus communicating its desire to develop closer ties with different 
communities throughout Québec. 


- To highlight the fact that the Y is first and foremost a philanthropic organiza- 
tion, the Y changed not only its name, but also its slogan and logo. The 
slogan, “Fulfilling lives”, serves as a reminder that we are a philanthropic 
organization enriching and impacting many lives. Our positioning campaign, 
“Do good for yourself. Do good for others,” conveys this same notion. Visit 
our new website at www.ymcaquebec.org and see for yourself. 


The charitable activities of the Y have garnered interest and raised curiosity 
throughout Québec. Future plans for the Y include increasing partnership 
opportunities in three key areas: education, health and community care, as 
well as the private sector. To be noted among the actions taken in 2008 was 
the partnership with Quebec City that led to the establishment of a YMCA 
day camp in the capital city. Also, in collaboration with Ubisoft, for the first 
time ever a YMCA daycare was implemented outside one of our centres. 


Finally, we look forward to extending our action into Cartierville. By breaking 
ground last November, we made official the unique partnership with the 
City of Montréal and the borough of Ahuntsic-Carterville, as well as the 
construction of a new Y centre to be opened in 2010. 


The success of our language school cannot be denied. In 2008, attendance 
reached new heights. Also, we made international gains thanks to a 
partnership with the Guatemala YMCA. There are many great projects on 
the horizon! 


The Y centres are firmly rooted in their communities and are admired for their commitment to 
2 humanitarian and social causes that promote the strengthening of communities. 
During uncertain economic times, this vision is more relevant than ever. 
The Y is, and will continue to be, a place for those in need, whether they be 
residents of Montréal or elsewhere. 


The YMCAs of Québec is strong and healthy. More and more people are 
interested in the Y and participate in its governance; yet another indicator of 
our success. 


7 
Caroline Sauriol, Stéphane Vaillancourt, 
Chair of the Board of Directors President and Chief Executive Officer 


Messa5e from the Foundation 


In 2008, The YMCAs of Québec Foundation once again improved the 
quality of life of thousands of individuals. 


Whether it be for a program such as Homework Help, the hiring of an 
animator for the children of refugees, or for social inclusion projects for 
seniors, more than $185,000 from the Endowment Fund was distributed to 
various community initiatives geared towards children, teens, seniors, or any 
other people in need. 


Our impact varied from the implementation of a family care program to the 
teaching of leadership skills and cooking to groups in the Youth Zone. 
Another of the Foundation’s initiatives saw Camp YMCA Kanawana welcome 
171 young campers from disadvantaged backgrounds, campers who might 
not otherwise have had the opportunity to make use of its facilities. This 
number represented 23% of all campers, a new record. 


In order to meet our goal of strengthening ties with the business community, 
the Y has established Ambassador-Breakfasts. These informal meetings, held 
over breakfast between the members of the board and business leaders, 
have allowed all participants to become better acquainted with The YMCAs 
of Québec, its operations and activities, and to establish strong relationships. 


Throughout the year, our valued committees composed of the members of the 
Board of Directors, external members, and volunteers, have supported our 
fundraising efforts. On this subject, the Foundation learned a great deal at the 
NAYDO conference in Montréal, where more than 1,100 professionals from 
YMCAs across North America and elsewhere gathered, all with an interest in 
philanthropy. Everyone had the unique opportunity to share their visions and 
strategies. 


Internally, we once again highlighted our philanthropic nature, which is at 
the heart of our positioning. We also made changes to our mission state- 
ment, which now reads as follows: “The YMCAs of Québec Foundation 
supports The YMCAs of Québec association and ensures its sustainability by 
promoting the impact of its community action, by collecting funds to 
support it, and by administering these funds responsibly.” 


Many thanks to all our donors, partners, staff, and volunteers. We are united in this important cause. 


Your commitment and passion inspire us. 


Against the backdrop of an economic recession, the needs of communities 
will undoubtedly be greater in 2009. We will have to rely on a stricter 
management of our resources and an increased collaboration on the part of 
all. Let’s keep our confidence high and continue supporting our Y; its mission 
and values are more relevant than ever. 


Mie . Lyn 


Michael Goldbldom Michael Novak

Philip likes the colour blue. The five-year-old boy stares

of soft rubber and picks out the blue ones from the lot 
before carefully placing them along the edge of the table 

Connie, his educator, engages him in conversation as the | 
joke around together. Then, Philip runs off to play as Marie- 
Héléne Navarra, his proud mother, happily looks on. Visibly, 
this child is full of life. He is beaming. 


“Would you believe that at age three, Philip was found to 
be moderately to severely autistic?” says his mother to an 
incredulous audience. “Today, in my eyes, he is cured.” 


Few children can overcome such an intellectual disabilityecsst 
One year ago, Philip’s vocabulary consisted of only three 
words. Today, he can communicate like any other child his 
age or thereabouts. Still, Marie-Héléne Navarra is reluctant 
to call this a miracle. She believes that his resounding 
success is owed to hours of therapy, faith, an unshakable 
determination, as well as a strong support network which 
includes the Notre-Dame-de-Grace Y centre. 


When he first came to the Y, Philip had a volatile and 
explosive temperament. Welcomed into a regular group, 

he gradually learned to listen more attentively, to 
communicate, and to not let his emotions get

{ From Westmount 
t Managua} 


Pablo St-André-Karass was just a child when he first stepped into 
the Westmount Y centre. Back then, he was in daycare. Now, some 
ten years later, he has just returned from an incredible trip to 
Nicaragua as part of the Y International Exchange Program, an 
experience that has had a profound effect on him. 


Now, some ten years later, he has just returned from a ale to 
the Y Int 


“Since my return, | see things differently,” says the grade 10 student 
from St. George’s High School. 


Pablo and seven other boys and girls between 15 and 17 years of 
age were chosen by the Westmount and Hochelaga-Maisonneuve 
Y centres to participate in a two-week stay in Managua, the capital, 
and in the rural communities of Boaca and Santa Lucia. The goal of 
this trip was to meet their peers from the YMCA of Nicaragua and to 
discuss common concerns such as water consumption, recycling, 
poverty, and the rights of children. The delegation stayed with host 
families. 


During his stay, Pablo participated in workshops, visited 

museums, and climbed mountains. However, it was while 
visiting the city that he experienced his first culturalshock. _ 
“It was just like in the movie Slumdog Millionnaire,” he 
says, still shaken by the memories. “I saw people living 
in homes made of garbage bags, or strewn together © 
with pieces of sheet metal”. Pablo also remembers the ~ 
pollution, the endless garbage dumps, and the half- — 
clothed children wandering about the trash looking for 
some supposed treasure. 


Nicaragua as part of ; 
Exchange Program, an experience that has had a profound effect « Lon n hi n 


Despite this display of poverty, Pablo has a soft spot 
for the country and for the kindness and warmth of 
the Nicaraguan people whom he refers to as the 
Nicas. He has also developed a strong friendship with 
Alex Medina, his counterpart from Managua. 


Pablo will see him again in December as it will be the 
turn of The YMCAs of Québec to receive the young 
“Nicas”. While Pablo can’t wait for them to see snow, 
he is worried about how they will react to all of our 
riches. “Sometimes | feel bad about how much we 
waste and | start to wonder about our Canadian way 
of life,” he admits. 


When asked what he learned during his stay in 
Central America, Pablo quickly responds: “I used to 
be ignorant. This trip has made me a better person.” 


Pablo St-André-Karass, 16 years old, Participant in the Westmount Y

Julian Lebensold, Member of the Downtown Y centre for 2 years 
Helen Neves, Coordinator, specialized in adapted physical activity 


{Giant 
steps } 


Julian Lebensold was never supposed to walk again. One day in April, 2006, this computer 
science professor from Vanier College found himself unable to move any of his limbs, The 
neurologist’s verdict was devastating: quadriplegia caused by a spinal cord lesion. This was 
a huge shock to Julian and his loved ones. 


Four months later, Julian felt a flicker of life in the tips of his toes. This highly improbable 
occurrence became his lifeline. His rehabilitation could begin in earnest. 


“l had been in a wheelchair for two years, and my rehabilitation at the Centre Lucie-Bruneau 
was coming to an end. | was looking for places to continue my training with a pool suited 
to my. physical condition,” states Mr. Lebensold. He and his physical therapist found that 
the Downtown Y centre’s facilities met his rehabilitation needs. “As a person with reduced 
mobility, being constantly faced with physical barriers completely changed my view of the 
world. | was glad to see that, at the Y, many of these barriers do not exist,” he says. 


y changed my view of the world. 
| was glad to see that, at the Y, many of these barriers do not exist.” 


The Y introduced the professor to Helen Neves, Coordinator, Group Fitness Programs, who 

supervises the Adapted Fitness Program at the Downtown YMCA. “Julian wanted to learn to 

walk again, but he could only stand up with assistance. He needed tailor-made exercises,” 

explains the Concordia graduate, Under her supervision and with her guidance, the sexage- 

narian began working out three days a week. “Helen always gives the impression of knowing 

exactly where she’s headed. Because she’s attentive, she knows when to stop and when to 
push me harder,” says Mr. Lebensold. 


After countless training sessions in the TechnoGym doing balance exercises 
and core strengthening, practicing walking on one of the Y’s simple 
accessibility ramps, as well as participating in Aquafit classes in the pool, 
- Julian progressed - all under the watchful eye of Helen and Vittia, a 
young volunteer at the Y. Within a few months, he was able to swap 

his wheelchair for a walker, and then the walker for canes. 


Julian was tenacious and never lost sight of his objectives. 
His next wish was to dance with his daughter at her December 
wedding. Once again, his wish came true. Incredibly, he can now 
walk with little or no assistance whatsoever. His next goal is to 
improve the distance he can walk before he needs a rest, 


“Family, friends, health professionals, the Downtown Y centre and its staff: 
| owe my rehabilitation to an exceptional support network and, | believe, to a lot 
of determination,” states Julian modestly, his eyes filled with joy.

Community Initiatives 


Health, Fitness and Recreation 
A new look for the YMCA 


The times have changed and the YMCA International Initiatives 
needed a new look to better reflect its persona- 
lity. The organization changed its name and logo, 
adopted a vibrant signature, and created new 
sub-brands to designate its fields of activity. The Y’s 
website was also completely redesigned. 


As a result, the YMCA of Greater Montreal changed its name to 
The YMCAs of Québec to meet the needs of the organization’s new 
development objectives. The YMCAs of Québec wishes to extend 
its action into communities throughout Québec and become the 
reference for well-being across the province. 


With a new visual identity, the Y also highlights its social and 
humanitarian mission. The “Y”, a distinctive YMCA symbol for many 
years, was kept. The new signature, Fulfilling lives, is dynamic and 
uplifting. It reminds us all that, first and foremost, The YMCAs are 
here to serve the community. 


THE YMCAs OF QUEBEC ee 


Strategic Vision 2009-2013 — Reaching out. Giving more. 


To remain relevant and ensure its sustainability, the YMCA completed a strategic planning 
process (2009-2014). This process required many internal and external consultations, as well 
as bidirectional communication with employees and volunteers. 


Cartierville Y centre: opening soon! 


In December, the Y’s management team and some friends of the Y helped 
break ground at the future site of the Cartierville Y centre. This fitness and 
community centre will offer a range of activities and services in order to meet 
the needs of the neighbourhood. The construction of this centre, the first new 
YMCA to be built in the last 20 years, was made possible by an exemplary 
partnership between the Government of Québec, the City of Montréal, the 
borough of Ahuntsic-Cartierville, and the YMCA. 


This $19.8 million project will be located on the corner of Laurentien 1 
Boulevard and de Louisbourg Street. The centre is expected to open in 
March 2010. 


2008 Peace Medal Awards Ceremony 


Five worthy individuals and three groups from Greater Montreal were 
awarded 2008 Peace Medals before more than 300 people. The individuals 
were as follows: Mrs. Marguerite Bilodeau, for her commitment as a‘nurse, 
artist, and activist; Mrs. Anne Farrell, for her work both here and abroad as 
an advocate for non-violence; Mr. Andy Rosenhek, for his philanthropic 
work overseas, and Mrs. Sharon Steinberg, for her role in the area of 
violence prevention. Musician Dan Bigras also received an honourary 
Peace Medal to highlight his tireless work with street kids, particularly 
with Refuge des jeunes. 


The groups awarded the Peace Medals were Artists for Peace, a peace 
organization from Québec; the Service d'aide et de liaison La Maisonnée, an 
organization helping with the integration of immigrants, and YAYA (Young 
Actors for Young Audiences), a socially-conscious theatre group. 


Thanks to our sponsors: The Alex and Ruth Dworkin Tolerance Fund, Centaure Cabinet de 
Services Financiers Inc., Konige Communications, Rotary Club of Montreal. 


{ FALfilling wes } 


Governance 


The Governance Committee, composed of volunteers from the Board of 
Directors, put a great deal of effort into reviewing the General By-laws of the 
Y and the roles and responsibilities of the member-partners. After having 
recommended the implementation of a recruitment plan, the YMCA signifi- 
cantly increased the number if its member-partners. 


Concrete actions taken by Human Resources 


Thanks to the Human Resources team, the centres had a number of resource: 
at their disposal to help facilitate the work of employees and volunteers. A new 
time management and pay system helped simplify the work of the centres, — 
while other resources helped improve decision-making during the hir 
process. Various initiatives concerning competency development 
succession planning were also implemented. 


The YMCA is mindful of providing a safe work environment and interest 
opportunities for personal and professional development. A 2007 survey 
showed an increase in overall employee satisfaction regarding working 
conditions and work environment, a sense of belonging to the organization, | 
and faith in the organization’s management. 


The YMCAs of Quebec: a management resource centre a 
for YMCAs in Eastern Canada e 


For many years, The YMCAs of Québec has been offering its support and 
services to the 13 YMCAs and YMCA-YWCAs located in New Brunswick, 
Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, as well as Newfoundland and Labrador. ; 
In 2008, The YMCAs of Québec offered its expertise in major project” 
development to eight YMCAs. Emphasis was placed on the training of 4 
employees and volunteers in Eastern Canada.

Adopt-A-School: Desjardins Assets 
Management and its partners still 
involved 


The 218 students from Marguerite-Bour- 
geoys school in the Centre-Sud district can 
now benefit from the first resource centre 
for mathematics, science, and technology 
in Montréal. The resource centre, which 
came at a cost of $54,000, is equipped with 
a wide range of state-of-the-art equipment. 
It is designed to encourage students to 
experiment and broaden their horizons by 
participating in learning activities as well as 
to stimulate their creativity and interest in 
mathematics, science, and technology. 


The Adopt-a-School program was launched 
in 2006 thanks to a partnership between 
Desjardins Assets Management and 
The YMCAs of Québec in an effort to 
promote equal opportunity. Managed by 
the Guy-Favreau Y centre, it offers financial 


_ support to primary schools in disadvan- 


taged neighbourhoods. To date, Desjardins 
Assets Management and its partners have 
adopted three schools from the Centre-Sud 
district and will have invested more than 
$800,000 over five years.

Strong Kids Campaign: 
Thank you, thank you, thank you! 


Through its initiatives, The YMCAs of Québec impacts the 
lives of some 100,000 individuals every year. By collecting 
$289,107, the 2008 Community Support Campaign helped 
improve the quality of life of thousands of children, teens, 
families, and seniors. 


The YMCA Residence and International Language School 
launched their first independent fundraising campaigns. 
The funds raised for the Residence were used to support 
integration programs for children and teens. Donations 
made to the Language School allowed three youths from 
disadvantaged socio-economic backgrounds to benefit 
from a three-week stay at the summer language day camp. 


Camp YMCA Kanawana: Objectives all but met 


In December, $1.48 million was collected for this unprece- 
dented environmental development project. The results 
encourage us to continue our efforts and collect the 
remaining $3.5 million to turn this dream into reality. 
Camp YMCA Kanawana will become a model ecological 
institution and will help raise the awareness of its young 
campers. 


The nature of the project and the quality of the camp’s 
programming explain in part the significant increase in 
camper registration, which rose from 80% capacity in 2007, 
to 91% in 2008. 


NAYDO: A huge success 


More than a thousand YMCA professionals from North 
America and around the world gathered at the NAYDO 
conference, held in Montréal between April 9-12, 2008, to 
talk about philanthropy and discuss ways in which it can 
be further promoted. The NAYDO conference strengthens 


.YMCA values by lending support to professionals and 


volunteers. in their philanthropic work through training, 
education, awareness, research, and knowledge sharing. 


Golf for a good cause 


The threatening weather did not discourage the hundreds 
of golfers gathered at the Pinegrove Country Club for the 
23” edition of The YMCAs of Québec Foundation’s Golf 
Tournament. Every year, golf enthusiasts enjoy themselves 
while supporting The YMCAs of Québec youth programs. 
Many thanks to the volunteers who lent a helping hand 
to the Foundation, and to our sponsors: GOLD, Services 
d’entretien Solmex; SILVER, SNC-Lavalin; BRONZE, Morin 
Relations publiques, CB Richard Ellis Québec Ltée, and 
Servicorp Industrial Supplies.

The YMCA Foundation Endowment Fund 
Making eyes light up 


Giving always comes from the heart and is inspired by the hope for a better and more 
just world. 


These generous gifts, from all corners of the province, ensure the sustainability of 
community initiatives and programs of The YMCAs of Québec - programs that have a 
ripple effect and allow new ones to be supported. 


On December 31* 2008, the value of the Endowment Fund stood at $4.675 million. 
This allowed the distribution of $207,380, of which $95,370 was allocated to various 
projects selected by the donors, such as Homework Help at the Pointe-Saint-Charles 
Y centre, support for the academic success of students aged 6 to 12, international 
programs, camper funds, and the development of Camp YMCA Kanawana. 


The Endowment Fund Committee also chose to allocate $88,635 to support the 
following projects: 


Winter Camping Downtown Y centre 
Youth Zone participants were introduced to winter sports and learned 
about ecological living. 


Covered Garden Downtown Y centre 
Hiring of an animator for children aged 0 to 5. 


Senior Contact Guy-Favreau Y centre 
Social inclusion program for seniors in the Centre-Sud district of Montréal. 


Health Through Sport Du Parc Y centre 
Program helping youth develop respect and a positive attitude through 
soccer and Taekwondo. 


Educational and Cultural Project Du Parc Y centre 
Program aimed at having youth participate in leadership activities, 
cooking classes, and dance. 


Youth Zones All centres 
Equipment and activities for these sites, where teens aged 
12 to 17 can meet and talk. 


Taking care of our volunteers 


Our volunteers are important. They enrich the lives of the 
Y and of the thousands of individuals they work with. Without 
them, many activities could not be offered. In order to 
strengthen employee-volunteer partnerships, a volunteer 
development plan was created and will be implemented 


over the next two years. 


THE YMCAs OF QUEBEC 


mmunity 
Initiatives 


Du Parc and Hochelaga-Maisonneuve Y centres: *} 


Repéres and Projet répit; don’t give up! 


The Y has set up two parallel initiatives to help teens 
who are having serious difficulties adapting to or fitting 
into their school environment. The Repéres and Projet 
répit programs have provided forty youths with per- 
sonalized academic support. Alternating between 
schoolwork, leisure and sports, and moments of 
reflection, these two programs are effective in redu- 
cing the number of school dropouts and in helping 
improve the self-esteem of teens. 


Guy-Favreau Y centre: Senior Contact flies solo 


The Guy-Favreau Y centre assigned the responsibility 
for Senior Contact, an intervention program for seniors 
in the Centre-Sud district who are at risk of isolation, 
to the community. The program, which reaches 2000 
seniors on a regular basis, is now being run by the 
Place Vermeil community centre. This much-needed 
program is jointly financed by The YMCAs of Québec 
Foundation and the Government of Canada. 


Hochelaga-Maisonneuve Y centre: 
Social participation program 


The Hochelaga-Maisonneuve Y cenire’s social partici- 
pation program is a one-of-a-kind project in Montréal. 
By pairing volunteers with intellectually disabled indi- 
viduals, the program encourages the latter to partici- 
pate in the activities of the centre, establish ties with 
the community, and develop greater autonomy. 


YMCA Residence for new arrivals: 
50¢ meals for three schools 


The food services program of the Residence of The 
YMCAs of Québec has partnered with community 
organization La Relance Jeunes et Familles to ensure 
that 100 healthy meals are prepared and served every 
day to children in three disadvantaged schools in the 
Centre-Sud district. The financial contribution of 
families is set at only 50¢ per meal. 


YMCA Residence for new arrivals: 
A drop-in childcare service 


Since the Residence of The YMCAs of Québec mainly 
welcomes families, it makes perfect sense for it to 
have a drop-in daycare service. In its first year, the 
Covered Garden welcomed 468 children under the 
age of 5. The service is crucial for asylum-seekers as 
it frees up some of their time, allowing them to get 
their affairs in order or participate in integration work- 
shops: 


Childre 


60" anniversary: The Notre-Dame-de-Grace Y centre’s 
nursery school flourishes 


Even after 60 years of existence, the Y’s creative nursery school 
program continues to prosper in Notre-Dame-de-Grace. Its suc- 
cess can be attributed to the ongoing support of families and to 
its unique framework. Happy anniversary and long live the nursery 
school! 


The Amazing Y Race for leadership development 


Seven teams, each composed of six young leaders and a youth 
worker from a Y centre, showed remarkable skill and speed 
during the first ever Amazing Y Race. The teams showed their 
leadership and teamwork skills in a challenging obstacle course. 
The Downtown Y centre team won this first edition and the race 
trophy is now proudly on display in the centre’s Youth Zone. 


Summer Work - Student Exchange 


More than 300 students aged 16 and 17 from all over Québec 
participated in the 6-week Summer Work - Student Exchange 
program, where they had the opportunity to do paid work in 
another Canadian province. The students were welcomed by 
families from elsewhere in Canada and vice-versa. It was an 
incredible opportunity to improve their second language, discover 
a new part of the country, and learn a new culture. 


Saint-Laurent Y centre: A new Youth Zone 


Teens at the Saint-Laurent Y centre now have their own Youth 
Zone, where they can participate in structured or free-time 


‘activities in a safe environment. Forty teens participate in the Zone 


on a regular basis. 


Du Parc Y centre: Opening of a new daycare 


The Du Parc Y - Ubisoft daycare provides services to both Ubisoft 
employees and the community at large. Born of a partnership 
between Ubisoft and The YMCAs of Québec, the subsidized 
daycare offers 80 spots at a reduced rate that are in addition to the 
hundreds of other spots offered in our other daycares. 


A YMCA day camp in Québec City: A first! 


Approximately fifty youths from the Saint-Roch district (borough of 
la Cité) inaugurated the first YMCA summer day camp in Québec 
City. This successful initiative, created in partnership with the Ville 
de Québec, will be taken up again in 2009. 


Hochelaga-Maisonneuve Y centre: 
An innovative partnership with the Botanical Garden 


For the first time, youth aged 6 to 14 from the Hochelaga-Maisonneuve 
Y centre had the opportunity to become budding horticulturists 
thanks to the help of Botanical Garden employees. Eight small 
garden plots were set aside for participants in the Montreal 
Botanical Garden’s Youth Garden program. 


Tandem Sud-Ouest in the primary schools: 
For well-informed youth 


Through the school component of its Projet jeune, Tandem 
Sud-Ouest raised the awareness of 1,418 students in the four 
Pointe-Saint-Charles and Little Burgundy primary schools in 
regards to street safety, emergency services, bullying, peaceful 
conflict resolution, and the potential dangers of the internet. 
No less than 80 presentations were offered to students in 
pre-kindergarten through grade 6. Tandem Sud-Ouest is a City of 
Montréal program managed by the Pointe-Saint-Charles Y centre. 


THE YMCAs OF QUEBEC 


palth, Fitness _ 
and Recreation 


Family membership: A success! 


In 2008, all Y centres offered a family membership. This 
membership gives members and their families access 
to a full range of recreational programming at a 
discounted rate. As a result, parent-child activities and 
child-only activities have seen a significant increase. 
The YMCA can boast helping parents take a break, 
while allowing them to adopt a healthy family lifestyle. 
Furthermore, in eight of the nine Y centres, families 
have access to new locker rooms specifically equipped 
to meet their needs. The gymnasiums are now 
equipped with dividing curtains that allow the increased 
use of the fitness facilities and a greater variety of 
programming. 


Member relations: Always looking to improve 
our service! 


In an effort to provide our members with the best 
possible service, the coordinators of the Downtown 
Y centre’s instructor-led classes organized two four- 
hour interactive training sessions on member relations. 
The positive feedback has encouraged us to renew this 
initiative in 2009. 


Physical fitness: Our facilities are worth 
their weight 


In 2008, to keep up with the latest in physical fitness 
trends and technology, the YMCA continued to update 
its cardiovascular and weight-training equipment. Our 
goal: to offer equipment that is ever more accessible, 
safe, reliable, effective, and invigorating. 


New health program for our members 


The YMCAs of Québec is conducting a study to assess 
the feasibility of implementing a new health program 
for the members of its fitness centres. This program 
would help members achieve their goals while signifi- 
cantly reducing their risk of quitting. Results from this 
study will be presented in the spring of 2009. 


A celebration for the West Island Y centre’s 20 years 


Last June, approximately 100 individuals, employees, 
volunteers, members, and residents celebrated the 
20" anniversary of the West Island Y centre. An open 
house and a reception marked this occasion, which 
allowed all these wonderful people to gather and share 
their memories or talk about future community projects. 
What a great day! 


2 


THE YMCAs OF QUEBEC 


ucation and 
Training 


YMCA International Language School: 
Panama exchange 


2008 was a busy year for the International Language 
School. Judging by the experience of a group of Pana- 
manians who came to perfect their teaching methods, 
the apprenticeship program designed by our pedago- 
gical team for teachers of English as a Second Language 
(ESL) it was a great success. The three ESL teachers 
all had a wonderful experience. Other countries have 
started to express an interest... 


In addition, the number of registrations for both the day 
and night classes at the Language School increased 
significantly in 2008, with French classes being the most 
popular. 


You Can Go: A program that can take you places 


Since March 2008, The YMCAs of Québec has followed 
the lead of many other YMCAs and organizations from 
coast to coast and joined the Canadian Post-Secondary 
Access Partnership. “You Can Go” targets groups that 
traditionally do not pursue post-secondary studies. 
It demystifies various aspects of post-secondary educa- 
tion and offers personalized support in the selection of a 
program of study and in obtaining financial aid. 


FIT: Fitness Instructor Training 


Centralizing the Fitness Instructor Training program is 
part of the Y’s new strategy to continuously improve 
service delivery and attract new clients. The YMCAs of 
Québec wishes to integrate new training and offer its 
classes in schools and other establishments. 


International Women’s Day: Gender and Development 


During International Women’s Day on March 8, 2008, 
30 individuals from the Y received training in how to inte- 
grate the “Gender and Development” approach in the 
workplace. The “GAD” approach aims to increase the 
participation of women in the decision-making process 
and encourages them to participate in the development 
of their community. Furthermore, nearly 400 women from 
all walks of life participated in the open house events 
offered by our fitness centres. 


ernational 
Initiatives 


Americas Social Forum: 
50 participants headed to Guatemala 


The 2008 ASF, a pilot project created in partner- 
ship with UQAM and The YMCAs of Québec, 
aimed to get approximately fifty students and 
representatives of civil society interested in 
philanthropy - particularly in the work being done 
with youth living in disadvantaged communities. 
The forum was held in Guatemala in October 
2008. 


The project was carried out in three phases, 
during which our delegates facilitated work- 
shops and participated in a panel on violence. 
This successful event encouraged many of the 
group’s participants to become volunteers for 
The YMCAs of Québec! 


Food sovereignty: A right for all 


During the Journées québécoises de la Soli- 
darité internationale, The YMCAs of Québec and 
Entraide Missionnaire, in partnership with the 
Collectif Educ-Action, presented a workshop 
at UQAM on the impact of food sovereignty 
patents. The lecturers showed the pitfalls of a 
free-trade agreement with Colombia that does 
not take into consideration either the Canadian 
parliamentry reports on that country's situation, 
nor the warnings of Canadian and Colombian 
human rights organizations. 


THE YMCAs OF QUEBEC 


Through its programs and 
activities, The YMCAs of 
Québec reached 100,000 
people. This social audit is 
made possible through the 
exceptional dedication of 
our 1,200 volunteers and 
our staff of 1,280. 


You and me against HIV/AIDS 


During World AIDS Day, The YMCAs of 
Québec and UNICEF jointly organized a 
youth forum to talk about this issue. More 
than 60 youths aged 12 to 17 took part in 
the event. By day’s end, the young partici- 
pants had drafted a declaration for the fight 
against AIDS. Called “II faut croire que |’on 
peut faire la difference”, this declaration 
outlines the youths’ commitment and their 
recommendations for teens, adults, schools, 
and governments. The day after the rally, a 
picture of the youths forming a vast human 
ribbon of solidarity made the front page of 
a Montréal daily. : 


Delegates from the Westmount and 
Hochelaga-Maisonneuve Y centres visit 
the Nicaragua ACJ: An unforgettable 
experience 


Eight young leaders from the Westmount 
and Hochelaga-Maisonneuve Y centres par- 
ticipated in a two-week exchange program 
with their partners from the Nicaragua 
YMCA. Activities and workshops focused 
_ on water waste, the environment, poverty, 
and the rights of children. The youths 
stayed with families in Managua and in the 
rural communities of Boaco and Santa 
Lucia. This visit had a tremendous impact 
on our delegates, who were experiencing 
Nicaraguan cultures for the first time.

Access for All Policy: A Y for Everyone 


For many years now, The YMCAs of Québec has implemented a flexible 
pricing system adapted to the income of its participants. Thanks to the 
Access for All policy, everyone can equally and fully benefit from the 
numerous programs and activities offered at their Y centre! In 2008, 
4,774 individuals received a total of $697,350 in financial assistance from 
the YMCA in order to participate in our programs. 


Innovation, Research and Development Fund: 
Concrete Results for the Community 


Created in 2003-2004 and financed entirely by The YMCAs of Québec, 
this fund aims to support new community initiatives. With $69,170 
at its disposal this year, the fund helped projects that, among others, 
developed a day centre for seniors at the Downtown Y centre, developed 
an educational kit for the outdoor education program at Camp YMCA 
Kanawana, and established a C-Vert program at the Hochelaga- 
Maisonneuve Y centre.
